extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and applicants preparing NIH grant applications (those considering including a cover letter)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to include a cover letter with an NIH grant application: requesting study section or IC assignment, describing needed expertise, identifying potential conflicts, and providing required submission information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest a particular review group for your application.
rubrics_metrics.description: You can request assignment to a particular study section (scientific review group, SRG) in a cover letter and explain why that study section would be the best fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate assignment requests are honored in the majority of cases. Use study section descriptions, recent study section rosters, and the NIH RePORTER database of funded grants to identify an SRG suitable for your application. Provide a clear rationale for why the requested SRG is a scientific match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest a particular institute or center (IC) for funding your research.
rubrics_metrics.description: If your research is relevant to more than one NIH IC, you can use a cover letter to suggest assignment to a specific IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate the types of research supported by different ICs using the NIH RePORTER database. Before requesting assignment to an IC in your cover letter, consult with program officers at that IC to determine whether your application is an appropriate scientific match.

rubrics_metrics.name: List the areas of expertise needed to evaluate your application.
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the scientific expertise needed to properly evaluate the application to help the SRG’s scientific review officer (SRO) assign appropriate reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about the domains, techniques, or perspectives that are essential for a fair review. Do not identify or name potential reviewers — recommending individuals raises bias concerns and usually places them in conflict with your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify potential reviewers who may be in conflict with your application.
rubrics_metrics.description: If someone may provide a biased evaluation of your application, inform the SRO in the cover letter and explain the nature of the conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the reason for the conflict (for example, a longstanding scientific disagreement). Note that similarity of research area, differing scientific opinion, or past participation on a panel for an unsuccessful application typically do not constitute conflicts. The SRO will use judgment to decide whether the explanation justifies placing that person in conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required information (late submissions, video files, pre-approvals).
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain situations require a cover letter, such as late application submission, plans to send video files, or application types (e.g., conference grants) that require pre-approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a pre-approval is required (e.g., for conference grants), include a copy of the approval letter with your submission. For a comprehensive list of situations that require a cover letter, consult the Create a Cover Letter webpage from NIH’s NIAID. Ensure required documentation is attached as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can see cover letters (confidentiality/access).
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letters are visible only to NIH staff with responsibilities relevant to application receipt, referral, and review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letters are not shared with other NIH staff or with peer reviewers; include in the letter only information appropriate for staff handling referral and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the PHS assignment request form (effective May 25, 2016) for assignment-related requests.
rubrics_metrics.description: A new PHS assignment request form (effective for due dates on/after May 25, 2016) provides a place to enter information needed to process requests for study section or funding institute assignment, expertise needed, and persons with potential conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of this form is required for your request to be brought to the attention of the appropriate review staff. Even with the new form, cover letters should still be used to provide information required for application submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow SF424 (R&R) Application Guide instructions for submitting a cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for submitting a cover letter as an attachment to your application are provided in the NIH SF424 (R&R) Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the cover letter according to the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide's procedures so it is properly received and associated with your application.
